name: io.hireeli/agent-test
title: Eli free Agent Test
description: Free, no-account Agent Test: where ChatGPT and Claude send a buyer, who wins, where agents get stuck

tools.name: agent_test
tools.description: Use this when the user asks whether AI agents like ChatGPT and Claude would buy from, choose or send buyers to a business, for example "Can ChatGPT buy from my store?", "Would an AI agent pick my company?", "Run the agent test on acme.com" or "Who does ChatGPT send my buyers to?", with their website given. It runs Eli's free Agent Test: ChatGPT and Claude each get real buying tasks in the company's market, and the result says where they sent the buyer, who got the sale instead and why, where an agent gets stuck on the site, the first fix, and the estimated sales going elsewhere. A result from the last 24 hours is reused; a fresh test takes one to three minutes, and when it takes longer the answer gives the page where it finishes live. Read-only: it changes no website, creates no account and contacts no one. Limitations: a few buying tasks on one day, not a ranking or a guarantee; only public pages are read; tests are limited per person and per day. Do not use it when no website is named (use who_ai_recommends) or for a person's own Eli workspace. It holds no account and cannot read, approve or change anyone's own Eli workspace.

website.description: The public website of the business, such as acme.com.

tools.name: scan_visibility
tools.description: Use this when the user asks for the full, raw AI-visibility scan of a public company website as data. It reads the site's public pages, checks whether AI search answers to a small sample of buyer questions in the company's category mention the company, and returns the complete scan result as JSON: overall score, visibility, readability and agent-usability scores, the buyer questions tested and the sources cited. Read-only: it does not change the website, create an account or contact anyone. Limitations: only public pages are read; the visibility figure comes from a small sample of questions and is not a ranking guarantee; a result can be reused from a cache for up to 7 days; a fresh scan can take a few minutes; requests are rate-limited per IP address with a daily limit; visibility is null when it could not be measured. Do not use it for a plain summary of one company (use test_company_for_ai) or for a person's own Eli workspace. It holds no account and cannot read, approve or change anyone's own Eli workspace.

domain.description: A public website domain or URL, such as example.com.

tools.name: test_company_for_ai
tools.description: Use this when the user asks what AI answers say about one named company, whether ChatGPT and other assistants name, recommend or understand it when buyers ask, and wants a plain summary instead of the raw scan, for example "Does ChatGPT recommend my company?", "What does ChatGPT say about my business?", "Is my business visible in AI search?" or "How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT?" with their website given. It leads with whether AI agents given a buying task sent the buyer to the company (from Eli's stored Agent Test of the site, where one exists) and what stops an agent on the site, then runs the same public scan as scan_visibility and groups the result into four parts: what AI can understand about the company, what AI can verify from cited sources, what actions AI agents appear able to take on the site, and the main gaps found. No account is needed. Read-only: it does not change the website, create an account or contact anyone. Limitations: only public pages are read; the result comes from a small sample of buyer questions and is not a ranking guarantee; a result can be reused from a cache for up to 7 days; a fresh scan can take a few minutes; requests are rate-limited per IP address with a daily limit; anything that could not be measured is marked [VERIFY: ...]. Do not use it when the user asks whether an AI agent would buy from or choose the business (use agent_test), when no company website is named (use who_ai_recommends) or for a person's own Eli workspace. It holds no account and cannot read, approve or change anyone's own Eli workspace.

url.description: A public company website domain or URL, such as example.com.

tools.name: who_ai_recommends
tools.description: Use this when the user asks who AI assistants recommend for a kind of service or product in a city, region or country, for example "Who does AI recommend for payroll software in the Netherlands?" or "Which accountants does ChatGPT recommend in Amsterdam?", usually to see whether their own business is among them. No website is needed. It asks AI assistants a small set of buyer questions about that service and place, with live web search, and returns the companies their answers recommended most often and the sources they cited. Do not use it to check one named company's website (use test_company_for_ai) or for a person's own Eli workspace. Read-only: it changes no website and contacts no one. Limitations: a small sample of answers on one day, not a ranking or a market share; the questions are worded for buying software or a service, so a very local trade can read oddly; a result can be reused from a cache for up to 7 days; a fresh check can take a minute or two; checks are limited per caller and per day, and the check says when Eli's free AI checks are switched off or used up. It holds no account and cannot read, approve or change anyone's own Eli workspace.

service.description: The kind of service or product buyers look for, such as "payroll software" or "wedding photographer".

location.description: The city, region or country, such as "Amsterdam" or "the Netherlands".

tools.name: roast_my_website
tools.description: Use this when the user asks where a website's homepage, or one of its pages, loses customers, or what to fix first on it, for example "Roast my website", "Why isn't my website converting?" or "What should I fix on my homepage?". It reads the public page and the site's public pages, checks how clearly they say what is sold, for whom, with what proof and what the next step is, and how readable they are for AI, and returns at most three concrete fixes, each with what Eli found. Do not use it for how AI answers treat the company (use test_company_for_ai) or for a person's own Eli workspace. Read-only: it changes no website and contacts no one. Limitations: public pages only; no visitor or sales data, so it says nothing about how many customers are lost; requests are rate-limited per caller. It holds no account and cannot read, approve or change anyone's own Eli workspace.

url.description: The page to check, such as https://example.com or example.com/features.

tools.name: why_competitor_wins
tools.description: Use this when the user asks why a competitor shows up in AI answers instead of their company, or which sources AI cites in their market, for example "Why does ChatGPT recommend my competitor instead of us?" or "Where does ChatGPT get its information about my market?". Give the company's website and, if known, the competitor's website or the category. It asks AI assistants a small set of buyer questions in that category, with live web search, and returns which companies the answers recommended, which source sites they cited (review sites, lists, forums, the companies' own pages), and which cited third-party pages name a competitor and not the company. Do not use it when no company website is named (use who_ai_recommends) or for a person's own Eli workspace. Read-only: it changes no website and contacts no one. Limitations: a small sample of answers on one day, not a ranking; a result can be reused from a cache for up to 7 days; a fresh check can take a minute or two; checks are limited per caller and per day, and the check says when Eli's free AI checks are switched off or used up. It holds no account and cannot read, approve or change anyone's own Eli workspace.

domain.description: The company's own website, such as example.com.

competitor_domain.description: The competitor's website, such as rival.com (optional).

category.description: What buyers search for, such as "payroll software" (optional; read from the website when not given).

tools.name: write_my_first_fix
tools.description: Use this when the user asks Eli to write the first fix for a website: the one page section or FAQ answer that answers a buyer question the site does not answer well yet, for example "Write the section my site needs to show up in ChatGPT's answers" or "What should my FAQ say so AI recommends us?". Give the website and the buyer question (or the gap). It finds the page on the site that best answers the question, says what that page is missing, and drafts the section from the site's own words, with anything it cannot verify marked [VERIFY: ...]. Draft text only: it never publishes, edits or sends anything anywhere. Do not use it to check visibility or a competitor (use test_company_for_ai or why_competitor_wins) or for a person's own Eli workspace. Without a question it uses the first buyer question a free scan of the website from the last 7 days showed the company was left out of. Limitations: public pages only; the drafted text needs Eli's free AI checks, which are limited per caller and per day; without them the answer says where the fix goes and what the page is missing, with no drafted text. It holds no account and cannot read, approve or change anyone's own Eli workspace.

domain.description: The company's own website, such as example.com.

question.description: The buyer question or gap to answer, such as "What is the best payroll software for startups in Europe?" (optional).

tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Use this when the user asks how to start with Eli for their website after a free check, or what Eli does. It says in plain words how Eli sells a company's products to AI agents and returns the links to start free for a website and to open its full report. Informational only: it does not create an account or change a website. Do not use it to check a website (use test_company_for_ai). It holds no account and cannot read, approve or change anyone's own Eli workspace.
